content.text: Switching the flow view to the students system to screenshot the chip variant.

Yes, there's a good way: put lookup ports on their own lane above the system boundary, not on the right rail with the write targets. I built two versions of that and checked both in Chrome on the students system.

**Today:** `ladok-api` is drawn as one more EXTERNAL write target next to `ad` and `iam`, with arrows from all three loaders and six crossing edges. It reads as "the loaders write to Ladok", which is wrong. The topology host already sends `direction: "lookup"`, but the flow view puts anything that isn't `in` on the output rail (`web/src/components/FlowView.tsx:1149`).

**Version 1: lookup lane with edges.** `ladok-api` sat above the boundary, centred over its consumers and labelled LOOKUP, with dotted two-headed edges into the top of each card. The right rail was clean (only `ad` and `iam`). The problem is that the three loaders share a column, so the edges stacked into one line running through the cards. It looked like a chain `ad-group-loader → student-account-loader → ad-membership`.

**Version 2 (what's in the tree now): lookup lane plus a chip on each card.** `ladok-api` stays in the lane, and each loader card gets a dashed `⇅ ladok-api` chip instead of an edge. Nothing crosses or stacks, and the main flow reads cleanly from the extractor through `ladok-events` to the loaders and out to `ad` and `iam`. The downside is that the chip takes header space, so the loader names now get cut off ("ad-group-lo…").

**My recommendation:** keep the version 2 layout, and draw the dotted lookup edges only when you hover or select the `ladok-api` card or a card that consults it. That shows the dependency when you ask for it without cluttering the flow. Two more fixes before shipping:
- Move the chip to a second line, or make it an icon with a tooltip, so names aren't cut off.
- Only show the new bottom connector dot on lookup cards. Right now every external card gets it.

The change is uncommitted and touches three files:
- `web/src/api.ts`: adds `'lookup'` to the port direction types.
- `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`: the lookup lane, the chips, and a LOOKUP label on the port card.
- `web/src/index.css`: dashed styling for the lookup card and chip.

The web build compiles. I haven't run any tests or added a test for the layout. The dashboard is still running from my scratch build on `http://localhost:8741` if you want to look.

Mostly yes, with one difference that I should fix in my proposal: the dashboard calls the command function itself and reads its JSON output, rather than calling a shared lookup function.

**How deploy works today.** The full body of `intropy deploy status` lives in `internal/deploy/status.go:34` as `deploy.Status(ctx, StatusOptions{...})`. That function takes `OutputFormat`, `Stdout` and `Stderr`. `cmd/intropy/deploy_status.go` is only a thin wrapper that reads the flags and calls it. The dashboard (`internal/dashboard/deploy.go`) calls the same `deploy.Status` with `OutputFormat: deploy.OutputJSON` and in-memory buffers. It then decodes the JSON the command printed, keeps its error message as is, and turns stderr into diagnostics. The comment there says why: the command already handles every case where the honest answer is subtle, and a second implementation would have to get all of them right again. ### Command verbs

One verb per meaning, used on every noun (`int`, `template`, `deploy`, ...).
The full set, grouped by what the verb does to the world:

**Read-only** — exit 0 even when the answer is "they disagree", never write
to git, never trigger a sync:

- **`list`** enumerates a collection: integrations on disk, templates in the
  library, published releases. It never prints one item's
  details.
- **`show`** prints the details of exactly one thing: a template's manifest,
  an integration's scaffold record. It never enumerates.
- **`status`** reports one component across every environment, one row
  each, and whether the rows agree. It never prints one environment's
  details — that is `show`.
- **`diff`** prints the rendered change a `sync` would apply, as the
  resources themselves. Both sides are committed revisions; it never diffs
  an uncommitted worktree.
- **`inspect`** prints the deployment model derived from one system topology:
  components, workloads, ports, and available local fixtures. It never
  renders manifests or writes project or Git state.
- **`render`** emits a complete Kubernetes YAML stream for one environment.
  It may ask for missing local fixture choices, buffers and validates the whole
  stream before writing stdout, writes all interaction and diagnostics to
  stderr, and never changes project, Git, or cluster state.

**Create or change project state** — may write files under the project.
Manifest creation may push a review branch, never the default branch:

- **`create`** makes something new from a template or from scaffolded
  parts: an integration, a system host, a release manifest to publish, or
  missing Kubernetes manifests on a GitOps review branch. Manifest creation
  accepts existing identical files but never replaces or deletes a file.
- **`add`** attaches something that already exists elsewhere to this
  project: a library registration. Unlike
  `create`, the content is pulled, not generated.
- **`update`** reconciles something installed against the ref its source
  now pins: a cached index against the registry. It never changes which
  ref is pinned — that is the publisher's job.
**Move or publish** — change what runs somewhere or what others can pull:

- **`publish`** pushes an immutable artifact to an OCI registry: a release
  manifest. What is published cannot be edited in
  place; a new version is a new publish.
- **`pin`** writes one component's image digest into one environment's
  overlay.
- **`promote`** copies the digests one environment runs into the next
  environment in the promotion graph.
- **`sync`** applies an environment's pending change through ArgoCD. It
  never decides what the change is — that is `pin` and `promote`.
- **`use`** selects which named customer context subsequent commands act

The catalog now lists each component's messages with their type and channel, and clicking one shows its real schema from the registry. I checked it in Chrome on the Uppsala workspace, and `go vet` plus the full Go test suite pass.

**One change from the plan:** the schema command is `intropy message show <ref> --schema`, not a new `message schema` command. AGENTS.md only allows a new command verb when no existing one fits, and `show` already means "print the details of one thing". A test enforces that rule. `--schema` can't be combined with `--output`, since it prints the schema exactly as the registry serves it.

**CLI**
- The `message list` and `message show` logic now lives in a new `internal/message` package. The cobra commands are thin wrappers around it, the same way the deploy commands wrap `internal/deploy`.
- The registry client can now fetch a schema version's document.
- New tests cover printing the schema, a message only the workspace declares, an unknown message, no registry configured, and `--schema` combined with `--output`.
- AGENTS.md now mentions `--schema`.

**Dashboard**
- New endpoint `GET /api/messages/{ref}` (in `internal/dashboard/messages.go`). It runs `message.Show` and `message.Schema` with JSON output and passes the commands' errors through unchanged, the way the catalog already calls `deploy.Status`.
- Successful answers are cached for the life of the dashboard process, since registry messages are released and versioned. Failures aren't cached, so a registry that comes back is picked up on the next click.
- Record paths are shown relative to the workspace instead of as absolute paths.

**Catalog**
- Publishes and Subscribes are now tables with one row per message: type, channel (`pubsub/topic`), contract, and a filter icon when the subscription filters on content. Long names wrap at the dots.
- The detail panel has three sections:
  - **Wire:** channel, contract, publishers and subscribers.
  - **Definition:** who declares the message, group, envelope, registry channels, and a link to the schema.
  - **Schema:** the host's own contract schema if the topology has one, otherwise the registry schema. Field descriptions now show under each field name.
- The placeholder schema is gone. For example, `invoice-created` now says it has no schema because only `domains/invoicing/invoicing/invoice-extractor` declares it and the registry doesn't.

**Customer names**
- `maxbo` became `fluxia` in the message test data. I also renamed `perfion-extractor` and `sbt-test-product-extractor-001` there, since they looked customer-specific.
- `organization: "Maxbo"` became `"Fluxia"` in the template end-to-end tests.
- `test-uppsala-integrations` became `test-fluxia-integrations` in the deploy and gitops tests.
- I left two things alone:
  - `acme` in README and `context_test.go`, which was already used as a placeholder there.
  - One comment in `internal/deploy/domain_test.go` that mentions "entrovia". The shared registry also has `io.intropy.entrovia.*` messages. Tell me if Entrovia is a customer and I'll change it.

**Things to know**
- Opening a message takes a couple of seconds the first time: it reads the registry's full export twice plus the schema. After that it comes from the cache.
- `internal/message` has no tests of its own; the CLI and dashboard tests cover it.
- Nothing is committed. All of this sits on `fix/registry-message-definitions` together with the earlier lookup-flow changes and your uncommitted registry work. The message refactor builds on that registry work, so it can't easily be split onto its own branch until that lands.
- The dashboard is still running from my scratch build at `http://localhost:8741`.
